changes.title: Hive: connect an Organization and share supported event, customer and purchase updates
changes.text: The Integrations page adds Connect, Reconnect and Disconnect for Hive, plus a clear description of the data shared. Backend jobs send supported event changes, customer contact and saved marketing preferences, and completed ticket purchases. A purchase does not subscribe a customer to marketing.
changes.impact: Organizations using the Hive pilot can keep supported Showpass data current without a manual send for every edit.
changes.limits: Requires integration-management permission, enable_hive_integration and configured Hive credentials. Initial event population remains operator-run. Purchase export supports completed, unadjusted ordinary ticket sales; mixed unsupported items and package child lines are excluded. Disconnect stops future sends but does not remove data already accepted by Hive. Hive processing and campaign revenue attribution were not tested.

qase.basis_or_limit: No Hive case was verified in the complete project search.
suggested_titles: Dashboard - Hive - Connect, reconnect and disconnect only the selected Organization
Core - Hive - Send supported Event and Customer updates without changing marketing consent
Core - Hive - Export completed eligible ticket sales once and exclude unsupported items

changes.title: Developer API keys: limit integration access and inspect request history
changes.text: Adds backend APIs to issue, list and revoke Organization-specific developer keys. A key is tied to an active employee and selected operations. The secret is returned once; expiry, revocation, current employee permissions, request limits and separate password-reading permission are enforced. Authorized employees can read retained request diagnostics.
changes.impact: Integrations can receive narrower access than a full employee login, and support can investigate requests without exposing the key secret.
changes.limits: This diff establishes backend capabilities, not a newly verified Dashboard management screen. Requires the new key schema, configured authentication and request-log storage in ClickHouse. Access to other Organizations and unsupported routes is rejected; live retention/configuration were not checked.

qase.basis_or_limit: No scoped developer-key or request-history case was verified.
suggested_titles: Core - Developer API Keys - Restrict access by Organization, employee and permitted operation
Core - Developer API Keys - Show request history only to authorized employees

changes.title: Webhook diagnostics hide credentials and unsafe receiver echoes
changes.text: Organizer-visible webhook diagnostics remove credential fields from nested data, redact sensitive headers, and strip credentials, query strings and fragments from destination URLs. Receiver response bodies are hidden when they could echo private request values.
changes.impact: Employees troubleshooting an integration have less opportunity to expose signing secrets or authentication data.
changes.limits: This is a change to diagnostic visibility. It does not prove every historical log, external receiver or monitoring destination has been sanitized.

qase.basis_or_limit: Delivery and log viewing are covered; credential redaction and unsafe receiver echoes are not asserted.
suggested_titles: Core - Webhooks - Hide credentials in delivery diagnostics and receiver responses

changes.title: Workflow approvers can preview ticket prices and fees
changes.text: The event preview opened from a publication-approval workflow adds Pricing & fees. It separates what the Customer pays from what the Organizer absorbs, with currency, calculation time and ticket-level fee details. The backend resolves the event through the authorized review and does not create an order.
changes.impact: Approvers can review the cost of a ticket without asking another team to calculate it or entering checkout.
changes.limits: Examples use the latest saved pricing for one online ticket paid by card. They are not frozen submitted prices, a whole-basket quote or a payout calculation. Configured-fee events are supported; payment-plan ticket types are marked unsupported.

qase.basis_or_limit: The existing legacy fee-calculator cases do not exercise a workflow reviewer’s Pricing & fees panel.
suggested_titles: Dashboard - Workflow Approval - Preview current saved ticket prices and fees without changing the request

changes.title: Workflow submissions retain the right review state, links and PDF answers
changes.text: Submission, withdrawal, approval and denial can reject an action based on an outdated review round. Notification jobs retain the intended round, suppress stale or duplicate sends, and build the review link with the correct workflow identifier. PDF choice fields show the selected labels instead of internal option values.
changes.impact: Reviewers are less likely to open the wrong submission or act on an old state, and submitted answers are easier to read.
changes.limits: Requires the paired backend and frontend workflow changes. Duplicate-email and concurrent-action behavior were not executed during this digest run; historical Jira comments are separate evidence.

qase.basis_or_limit: Saved cases explicitly check autosave/submit ordering, new review rounds, original notification snapshots and readable selected PDF answers.

changes.title: Custom messages explain an unannounced event date or time
changes.text: Adds separate messages for an unknown date-and-time and an unknown time on a known date. Ticket Type overrides take priority over Event overrides, then Organization defaults. Customer-facing schedule data carries the resolved message into supported pages, orders, emails and wallet-update paths. The newer frontend now carries the saved messages through Event details, discovery, Box Office, group sales, My Orders and Upcoming Events. Photo Ops retain pending-time wording; explicitly classified Autograph, Selfie and Other experiences omit it while preserving their date and confirmed schedule.
changes.impact: An Organizer can explain when scheduling information will be announced instead of showing only a generic TBD label.
changes.limits: Messages are trimmed and limited to 256 characters; a blank override falls back to the next setting. Requires the Venue/Event/Ticket Type migrations and compatible clients/workers. Live wallet delivery and every client were not tested. Jira still says On Deck despite code on develop. Experience-specific suppression requires the backend experience_type classification; older responses retain ordinary Event behavior.

qase.basis_or_limit: Checks announcement-message edits resetting a review; does not check inherited text, length validation or Customer displays.
suggested_titles: Core - Event Dates - Apply Organization, Event and Ticket Type announcement messages with correct inheritance
Core - Experience Schedules - Show pending-time messages for Photo Ops and omit them for other Experience types

changes.title: Shared ticket Inventory protects reserved quantities and overall Capacity
changes.text: Adds backend and Admin support for several Ticket Types to share one Event Capacity. Each Ticket Type can have a protected quantity and an optional maximum. Basket and waitlist admission checks account for the shared pool; resale and held-allocation changes avoid counting or returning the same places twice.
changes.impact: A configured Event can share unsold places across ticket categories while protecting reserved allocations.
changes.limits: Pools belong to one concrete Event occurrence and Organization; a recurring parent is not a valid owner. Management requires Manage Events permission. No new Dashboard pool editor was established in the frontend diff. Concurrent purchases, resale completion/cancellation and physical admission were not executed.

qase.basis_or_limit: Existing package Capacity and Hold controls do not configure shared Ticket Type pools or protected quantities.
suggested_titles: Core - Shared Ticket Inventory - Enforce combined Capacity, protected quantities and Ticket Type maximums
Core - Holds - Restore a reduced or expired claim to its parent allocation exactly once
Core - Resale - Preserve the original Hold allocation when replacement tickets sell

changes.title: The public guest-list form moves to the newer interface
changes.text: Adds a public guest-list page with widget-specific fields, event selection, birthday handling, manual entry and Facebook import. The form prevents a second submission while a request is pending, shows field errors and confirms a saved request. The server checks the widget, Organization, available Event and guest-count limits before saving a pending reservation. Follow-up layout changes separate Facebook import from manual entry and add submit-button spacing. Loading placeholders now match the centered import control, separator and submit area in the loaded form, including translated labels. Placeholder controls are disabled and excluded from keyboard navigation.
changes.impact: Visitors have a clearer signup flow, while a rejected or unsaved request is not counted as a successful registration.
changes.limits: Existing embedded links switch only when enable_public_guestlist_nextjs_embed is active for the Venue; otherwise they keep the legacy form. A saved guest-list request is pending, not confirmed admission. Required custom questions are enforced by the client; server validation checks supplied answer values. This run did not submit a guest-list request.

qase.basis_or_limit: Guest-list submission, closed dates and booking limits exist; legacy/new-form rollout coexistence is not explicit.
suggested_titles: Widget - Guest List - Keep legacy booking working with rollout off and the accepted new form with rollout on
Widget - Guest List - Match loading placeholders to the form in English and French

changes.title: Organizer profiles keep Queue-it protection during page navigation
changes.text: The public Organization data exposes its configured Queue-it setting, and the newer Organizer profile loads the existing queue integration when eligible. Client-side route changes recheck the protected destination after Queue-it configuration is ready.
changes.impact: Moving between public pages within the app does not rely solely on the queue check from the first full page load.
changes.limits: Applies to configured Queue-it Organizations and supported protected pages. The provider configuration must be available; readiness errors are recorded. No live queue challenge or admission test was run.

qase.basis_or_limit: Cases explicitly cover direct entry, first protected client navigation, return/admission reuse and existing Event/website conditions.

changes.title: Bandsintown activation records cost acceptance and checks fee setup
changes.text: The legacy Integrations page adds an Organizer enablement flow. The server verifies or provisions the applicable Bandsintown fee configuration before enabling the Venue. Disablement is restricted to an authorized Admin.
changes.impact: An Organization can accept the integration cost explicitly rather than enabling it with an incomplete or conflicting fee configuration.
changes.limits: This is opt-in/disablement work, not proof that all event publishing or reporting phases of the Bandsintown integration are complete. The fee selector covers eligible ticket sales on Web, Widget and Mobile, with specified payment types. Conflicting fee cards block activation; no setting was changed here.

qase.basis_or_limit: No Bandsintown activation or disablement case was verified.
suggested_titles: Dashboard - Bandsintown - Require fee setup and cost acceptance before activation
Core - Bandsintown - Allow only Admin to disable an active integration

changes.title: Seasonal membership revenue stays with eligible benefits and preserves rounding
changes.text: New seasonal allocation work uses the applicable group-level benefits rather than adding membership-level benefits into the same split. Revenue and fee distribution respect each eligible benefit’s allocation and retain cent-level totals. Existing allocation records retain their legacy eligibility.
changes.impact: Finance reporting is less likely to split a season-pass purchase into an unintended benefit or distribute more than its allocated share.
changes.limits: This concerns seasonal membership revenue allocation, not the member’s admission rights. Existing records are not described as a blanket historical repair. Financial reconciliation and new-season processing were not executed.

qase.basis_or_limit: Eligible benefit/event splits are asserted; uneven rounding and exclusion of ineligible allocations need explicit protection.
suggested_titles: Core - Membership Revenue - Allocate only eligible benefits and preserve the full amount after rounding

changes.title: Voucher Refunds restore combined uses across refunded order lines
changes.text: When a Refund includes several order lines that used the same voucher, their uses are combined and added back to the voucher allowance on a freshly locked record. The cached balance is cleared after commit. This Refund change does not restore voucher uses for Dashboard Void.
changes.impact: Refunded FlexPass/voucher uses are less likely to remain unavailable when several Event lines are refunded together.
changes.limits: Requires enable_voucher_refund_limit_fix. The previous path remains when the switch is off. No live voucher balance or refund was changed, and switch state is unknown.

qase.basis_or_limit: Needs review: one-ticket discount case allows either acceptance or rejection after reversal. It does not prove combined voucher usage is restored across order lines.
suggested_titles: Core - Voucher Refunds - Restore combined usage across refunded order lines with the rollout switch enabled

changes.title: Package exchange calculations use credit at the matching order-line scope
changes.text: Refund/exchange calculations use the credit amount recorded at the same reporting scope as the order line’s totals. Package parents include child credit without taking an unrelated child-only amount a second time.
changes.impact: The amount available during a package exchange is less likely to be understated or counted at the wrong level.
changes.limits: This source change does not establish a general refund entitlement or a verified final payment amount. No Exchange, Refund or credit record was created.

qase.basis_or_limit: Package fee adjustments and credited Exchanges exist separately; matching package order-line credit scope is not explicit.
suggested_titles: Core - Package Exchanges - Apply credit at the matching order-line scope

changes.title: Resale waitlists continue to later buyers when the first request cannot fit
changes.text: The scheduler considers subscribers in queue order but continues when a buyer has no compatible resale supply or complete quantity match. That buyer stays pending while a later compatible buyer can be considered.
changes.impact: A request that cannot currently be filled no longer stops all later compatible resale requests.
changes.limits: Complete resale submissions are still matched together; this is not permission to split every listing or skip an eligible buyer. Background scheduling and customer emails were not run.

qase.basis_or_limit: Manual FIFO allocation expects a later fitting buyer to remain Pending. Its applicability to resale matching needs review; it is not proof of the new skip-and-continue behavior.
suggested_titles: Core - Resale Waitlists - Skip an incompatible earlier request and fulfill the next compatible buyer

changes.title: Upgraded tickets can still offer their configured upsells
changes.text: An upgraded ticket is no longer excluded solely by its replacement marker when finding its currently configured upsell paths.
changes.impact: Customers using an upgraded ticket can be offered eligible extras rather than losing the upsell path because an upgrade occurred.
changes.limits: Existing basket, package, seating and sale validation still apply. No upgrade or additional purchase was executed.

qase.basis_or_limit: Ticket replacement on upgrade is asserted, but keeping eligible upsell offers is not.
suggested_titles: Core - Ticket Upgrades - Keep eligible upsells after replacing the selected ticket

changes.title: Admin schedule editing uses the Event or Venue’s local time
changes.text: Shared Admin fields resolve entered local dates and times using the relevant timezone, retain the intended local schedule and report invalid or conflicting changes. Event and membership schedule forms use the shared handling, including Admin history/reconciliation paths.
changes.impact: An Admin editing a season or Event schedule has clearer local-time controls and fewer opportunities for the stored time to disagree with the entered schedule.
changes.limits: Timezone policy and rollout configuration still govern resolution. Repeated or nonexistent daylight-saving times require the supported handling; this run did not save an Admin form or test a clock-change boundary.

qase.basis_or_limit: No matching Admin schedule-editing case was verified.
suggested_titles: Admin - Schedules - Save Event and Venue dates in their configured local timezone

changes.title: Box Office postal answers can populate the normal Customer postal field
changes.text: For eligible staff Box Office sales, a valid purchaser postal answer can fill a missing invoice postal address and update the linked Customer address. The code recognizes the built-in purchaser postal value or one unambiguous valid postal/ZIP text answer. Will Call export can fall back to the invoice’s postal code when the guest value is blank.
changes.impact: Collected postal information can appear in the normal Customer address and standard reporting rather than remaining only a custom answer.
changes.limits: This adds backend mapping, not a new standalone postal input. Existing invoice postal values are preserved. Eligible saved purchaser data is used; individual Attendee answers are not treated as the buyer’s address. Jira is still On Deck; no sale or Customer was changed.

qase.basis_or_limit: Shipping and profile-address cases do not prove mapping the Box Office purchaser postal answer to the Customer address.
suggested_titles: Box Office - Customer Details - Save purchaser postal answers to the Customer postal field

changes.title: Box Office delivery details use the Event timezone
changes.text: Delivery-date formatting prefers the Event timezone supplied on the basket line and falls back to the existing timezone only when it is absent.
changes.impact: An Event held in a different timezone from the Organization is less likely to show conflicting times between the cart and delivery details.
changes.limits: This is a display correction. It does not reschedule the Event, and no checkout was executed.

qase.basis_or_limit: Covers a device timezone different from the Venue; a distinct Event timezone override is not explicit.
suggested_titles: Box Office - Delivery - Show the Event timezone when it differs from the Venue and device

changes.title: Embedded Events List improves contrast, keyboard focus and retry
changes.text: The legacy embedded Events List updates its accessible presentation and Load more behavior. A keyboard user retains a focus target while loading; completion restores useful focus, and a failed page request can be retried instead of permanently ending pagination.
changes.impact: Visitors using keyboard navigation or needing clearer contrast have a more usable embedded list.
changes.limits: Applies to the legacy embedded Events List, not every public listing. Contrast, screen-reader announcements and keyboard behavior were source-reviewed but not browser-tested.

qase.basis_or_limit: No matching legacy embedded Events List accessibility and recovery case was verified.
suggested_titles: Widget - Events List - Keep readable contrast, visible keyboard focus and a usable retry

changes.title: Photo Ops pages show clearer prices, biographies and mobile information
changes.text: Talent pages shorten desktop biography presentation, omit empty Information content, and show a clearer base-price/currency/fee explanation. Related copy uses Photo Ops and Autographs & More; autograph/selfie bookings omit an unhelpful standalone Time TBD label. Talent filters extend across the page, and mobile names, subtext and day badges use larger defined text sizes.
changes.impact: Customers can reach the available experiences sooner and better understand the price and useful details on smaller screens.
changes.limits: These are changes within the Photo Ops/Talent flow, not evidence that the full Photo Ops product is launched. Ordinary confirmed times and the full unknown-date fallback remain. Browser responsiveness and purchase completion were not tested.

qase.basis_or_limit: Custom-website Experience purchase checks session and price; biography layout, fee information and mobile presentation are not covered.
suggested_titles: Public Web - Photo Ops - Show readable biography, fee information and mobile offering details

changes.title: Experience quantities use the experience selection flow
changes.text: Public cart and checkout Review show an experience ticket’s current quantity as text rather than exposing the generic quantity dropdown or increment control. Ordinary admission tickets and Product Extras retain their quantity controls. Edit and Remove actions are aligned together in the legacy cart.

setup_notes: Staff Refund: the Employee needs Administer Transactions and access to the chosen refund type. Use a paid voucher-discounted order with Refund offered in Dashboard → Transactions. If the voucher covers the entire purchase and Refund is unavailable, that order cannot run the staff Refund check. Do not replace Refund with Void or Return free tickets.

Customer free return — Organization setting: a setup administrator with permission to change Venues opens Admin → Venues, searches for the Organization name and opens its matching Venue. Record the original Allow free return value, set it ON and save. This is the saved Venue field allow_free_return, not the Customer Self Refund Settings control or the voucher-fix switch.

Customer free return — each Ticket Type: an Employee with Manage Events opens Dashboard → Events → Manage Events → the Event → Ticket Types → edit the Ticket Type. Under Basic Info → Inventory display, set Allow free ticket returns to Allow Free Returns and save. Reopen it to check the saved value. This control is hidden until the Organization setting above is ON. An explicit Ticket Type choice overrides the Event choice; Use Event Settings inherits the Event value, then the Organization value if the Event has no override. For this check, select Allow Free Returns explicitly on all 3 Ticket Types.

Customer free return — time and tickets: choose future, in-person Events starting later than the Venue’s Automated return window (hours), found on the same Admin → Venues record. Use ordinary downloadable tickets already delivered to the buying Customer, unscanned and not previously returned, transferred or listed for resale. Do not use shipping, online Events, physical scan cards, Customer-activation-only delivery or tickets hidden from confirmation email. Use only the voucher discount, with no extra discount or stored money credit. The Customer must own the order.

Customer free return — starting screen and finish: in that Customer’s My Orders, open the $0 order’s options and check that Return free tickets appears and all 3 intended tickets can be selected. If the option or required ticket selection is unavailable, mark this check Blocked and record which setting or ticket condition is missing. The setup owner supplies the normal background-processing deadline; a submitted request alone is not a completed return.
